title.value: On the Transfer of Object-Centric Representation Learning
title.justification: The title is found at the top of the paper and clearly states the main focus of the research, which is about the transferability of object-centric representation learning.
title.quote:
Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025

ON THE TRANSFER OF OBJECT-CENTRIC REPRESENTATION LEARNING

analysis.description: The paper investigates the transferability of object-centric representation learning methods to unseen datasets and introduces a benchmark for measuring zero-shot performance. It also proposes a novel fine-tuning approach for adapting pre-trained vision encoders, showing improved performance in object discovery across diverse datasets.

type.justification: The paper involves experiments with object-centric models on various datasets to evaluate their transferability and proposes a new fine-tuning method, indicating an empirical study.
type.quote: Thus, in this work, we answer the question of whether current real-world capable object-centric methods exhibit similar levels of transferability by introducing a benchmark comprising seven different synthetic and real-world datasets.

name.justification: The paper addresses visual scene decomposition and object discovery, which are central topics in the field of Computer Vision.
name.quote: The goal of object-centric representation learning is to decompose visual scenes into a structured representation that isolates the entities into individual vectors.

name.justification: The paper deals with deep learning models for object-centric representation learning, which falls under the broader category of Deep Learning applications.
name.quote: These so-called foundation models can be applied to a variety of data and tasks in a zero-shot manner.

name.justification: The paper focuses on unsupervised object discovery and representation learning without labeled data.
name.quote: results in state-of-the-art performance for unsupervised object discovery, exhibiting strong zero-shot transfer to unseen datasets.

name.justification: DinoSAUR is highlighted as a foundational model for object-centric learning in this study and is subjected to further fine-tuning for improved performance.
name.quote: We propose a finetuning approach applied to DINOSAUR, which allows the stable adaptation of the parameters of the pre-trained encoder for the task of object discovery.

is_contributed.justification: DinoSAUR itself is not a new model introduced in this paper, but rather an existing model that the paper builds upon.
is_contributed.quote: Building on the DINOSAUR model (Seitzer et al., 2023), our proposed finetuning approach sets a new state-of-the-art for real-world object-centric learning.

is_executed.justification: The paper involves the execution and fine-tuning of DinoSAUR for the object discovery task.
is_executed.quote: Building on the DINOSAUR model (Seitzer et al., 2023), our proposed finetuning approach sets a new state-of-the-art for real-world object-centric learning.

is_compared.justification: DinoSAUR is compared numerically to other models such as SlotDiffusion and SPOT in the experiments reported.
is_compared.quote: SlotDiffusion and DINOSAUR are on par in terms of FG-ARI, while SlotDiffusion achieves the best mBO.
